name: AI Risk Shield Comprehensive Regulatory & Governance Knowledge Base

evidence_levels.Level_1: Official EU & National Regulations (EU AI Act, GDPR/RODO, DORA, NIS2, EU Copyright)
evidence_levels.Level_2: International Standards & Security Controls (NIST AI RMF 1.0, ISO/IEC 42001, ISO/IEC 27001, KNF)
evidence_levels.Level_3: Cybersecurity Vulnerability Catalogs (OWASP Top 10 for LLMs)
evidence_levels.Level_4: Industry Best Practices & Enterprise AI Architectures

regulatory_references.title: AI Literacy Obligation
regulatory_references.summary: Providers and deployers of AI systems shall take measures to ensure, to their best extent, a sufficient level of AI literacy of their staff, taking into account their technical knowledge, experience, education, and training.

regulatory_references.title: High-Risk AI Systems Classification (Employment & Worker Management)
regulatory_references.summary: AI systems intended to be used for recruitment, screening, candidate evaluation, performance monitoring, or employee task allocation are legally classified as High-Risk AI Systems.

regulatory_references.title: Risk Management System for High-Risk AI
regulatory_references.summary: High-risk AI systems must establish, implement, document, and maintain a continuous risk management system throughout their lifecycle, identifying known and foreseeable risks.

regulatory_references.title: Data Governance & Training Data Quality
regulatory_references.summary: High-risk AI systems utilizing model training must be developed with data governance and management practices covering dataset design, bias examination, and data mitigation.

regulatory_references.title: Technical Documentation
regulatory_references.citation: EU AI Act Article 11 & Annex IV
regulatory_references.summary: Technical documentation for high-risk AI systems must be drawn up before system release to demonstrate compliance and provide authorities with necessary verification data.

regulatory_references.title: Human Oversight
regulatory_references.summary: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed in such a way that natural persons can oversee their operation, prevent or minimize risks, and override output.

regulatory_references.title: Accuracy, Robustness & Cybersecurity
regulatory_references.summary: High-risk AI systems shall be resilient against errors, adversarial prompt injection attacks, and unauthorized system access.

regulatory_references.title: Obligations of AI Integrators and Providers
regulatory_references.summary: Any entity that modifies an AI system, fine-tunes models, or integrates LLM APIs into commercial products assumes the legal obligations of an AI Provider.

regulatory_references.title: Transparency Obligations for Customer AI Systems
regulatory_references.summary: Providers must ensure that AI systems intended to interact directly with natural persons (chatbots) or generate synthetic content clearly inform users of AI generation.

regulatory_references.title: Data Processing Agreements & Security of Processing
regulatory_references.summary: Data controllers must execute Data Processing Agreements (DPA) with third-party AI vendors and implement measures to prevent confidential data exposure to public models.

regulatory_references.title: Digital Operational Resilience Act (ICT & AI Risk Management)
regulatory_references.summary: Financial entities must manage ICT third-party risk, including AI vendors and cloud models, establishing continuous security testing and incident reporting.

regulatory_references.title: Cybersecurity & Supply Chain Risk Management
regulatory_references.summary: Essential and important entities must address supply chain security, including vulnerabilities resulting from third-party AI software integrations.

regulatory_references.title: Text & Data Mining (TDM) & Commercial IP Protections
regulatory_references.summary: Governs the use of copyrighted content in AI model training, dataset extraction, and commercial deliverable ownership rights.

regulatory_references.title: Artificial Intelligence Management System (AIMS)
regulatory_references.summary: Provides requirements for establishing, implementing, maintaining, and continually improving an Artificial Intelligence Management System within organizations.

regulatory_references.source: NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
regulatory_references.title: NIST AI RMF Core Functions (GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE, MANAGE)
regulatory_references.summary: Comprehensive framework for managing AI risks to individuals, organizations, and society through four core governance functions.

regulatory_references.title: Komunikat Chmurowy KNF & AI Risk Standards
regulatory_references.summary: Regulatory requirements for Polish financial institutions utilizing cloud services, SaaS AI tools, and outsourced model processing.

regulatory_references.title: LLM01: Prompt Injection Vulnerability
regulatory_references.summary: Occurs when untrusted user inputs manipulate an LLM's context, altering system behavior or executing unauthorized actions.

regulatory_references.title: LLM02: Sensitive Information Disclosure
regulatory_references.summary: Occurs when an LLM reveals confidential data, PII, source code, or proprietary algorithms through output responses.

regulatory_references.title: LLM06: Excessive Agency & Unchecked Automation
regulatory_references.summary: Granting excessive permissions or autonomous action capabilities to LLM agents without human oversight mechanisms.
